evals.prompt: Our notifications code is spread over NotificationService, NotificationFormatter, NotificationChannelFactory, EmailSender, SmsSender and a NotificationPreferencesHelper — callers in 14 places call 3-4 of these in sequence. I want to redesign the interface so it's easier to test and for agents to navigate. How should I shape it?
evals.expected_output: Uses the deep-module vocabulary to propose collapsing the cluster behind a small interface at a clean seam, justified via depth, leverage, locality and the deletion test.
expectations: Uses the terms module, interface, depth, seam and adapter consistently, and avoids 'component', 'service' or 'boundary' as design vocabulary
Applies the deletion test to at least one of the existing classes (e.g. would deleting the Formatter or Helper concentrate or just move complexity)
Frames benefits in terms of leverage for the 14 callers and locality for maintainers
Treats EmailSender/SmsSender as adapters at a seam and notes that two adapters make it a real seam
States that tests should go through the new interface (the interface is the test surface) rather than testing internal parts

evals.prompt: I'm about to add a `PaymentGateway` interface in front of our Stripe calls so the order module is testable. Right now Stripe is the only provider and we have no plans for another. Is putting a port there the right seam, and how should tests work?
evals.expected_output: Classifies Stripe as a true-external dependency and justifies the port by the production + test-mock adapter pair, applying seam discipline.
expectations: Classifies Stripe as a 'true external' dependency (the fourth dependency category) that is injected as a port with a mock adapter in tests
Applies 'one adapter means a hypothetical seam, two adapters means a real one', counting the test adapter as the second adapter
Recommends the order module accept the gateway as a dependency rather than constructing it internally
Recommends asserting on observable outcomes through the order module's interface rather than internal state

evals.prompt: We've decided to deepen the `ReportExporter` cluster (CSV, PDF and XLSX exporters plus a shared column-mapping util and a ReportQueryBuilder that hits Postgres). Can you explore a few alternative interfaces for the deepened module before we pick one?
evals.expected_output: Follows the Design It Twice pattern: frames the problem space, spawns 3+ parallel sub-agents with differing constraints, then compares on depth, locality and seam placement and gives an opinionated recommendation.
expectations: Frames the problem space (constraints, dependencies with their category, rough illustrative sketch) before designing
Plans to spawn 3 or more parallel sub-agents each with a different design constraint (e.g. minimise interface, maximise flexibility, optimise for the common caller, ports & adapters)
Classifies the Postgres dependency as local-substitutable (e.g. PGLite) or otherwise names its dependency category
Compares the designs on depth, locality and seam placement
Gives an opinionated recommendation (possibly a hybrid) rather than just a menu
